context:
The heatmap is a single component with no internal state beyond
selection. All data comes from the summary prop. Filter controls
live in BenchmarkIndex and drive the (sf, phase) → artifact URL
selection + client-side filtering of rows by tuning/trust.

For coloring: write a pure function colorForCell(ms, minInCol,
maxInCol) → CSSValue. Unit-test it directly with known inputs before
wiring it to the component. The color math is where a proposal most
easily goes wrong; keep it isolated and snapshot-tested.

For the log-ratio color: clamp the ratio at 10x so a 100x-slower
outlier doesn't compress everything else. Values above the clamp
still render red but don't stretch the scale further.
description:
The strategy review (2026-04-15) concluded that the explorer's primary
surface per benchmark must be a Platform × Query matrix leaderboard,
modelled on ClickBench but adapted to BenchBox's multi-dimensional data
(trust tiers, tuning modes, phases). The current BenchmarkIndex.tsx
renders a sorted list - this TODO replaces it with the matrix.

The matrix is the product definition: arriving at /results/tpch/ should
immediately answer "which engine wins, and by how much, on each query?"
without navigating further.

Layout:

  [Scale ▾] [Tuning ▾] [Phase ▾] [Trust ▾]  [View: Matrix | List]

  Platform      Trust    Power/Geomean  Cost   Q1    Q2   ... Q22
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  DuckDB        maintainer   3184.9 / 11.5ms  $0    18ms  4ms  ... 6ms
  Polars        maintainer   --     / 8.2ms   $0    12ms  3ms  ... 4ms
  DataFusion    community    2847.1 / 13.7ms  $0    22ms  6ms  ... 9ms

Heat coloring rules (corrected from the original proposal):

- Per-column normalization (each query independently).
- **Log scale**, not linear - SQLite at 892ms vs DuckDB at 11ms would
  collapse the DuckDB/Polars/DataFusion gradation under linear.
- Scale is **ratio-to-fastest-in-column** (ClickBench-style),
  not min-max.
- Null cells render "-" in muted gray with `aria-label="no data"`.

Row selection: checkboxes on each row feed the existing Compare page
via URL-encoded IDs. See explorer-compare-url-short-ids for the ID
encoding concern.

anti_patterns.dont: default the ranking metric to geomean_ms for TPC-H/DS
anti_patterns.why: those benchmarks define power_score as the standard metric
dark mode and high-contrast accessibility settings need to override

anti_patterns.instead: render them with a visible tier badge instead
anti_patterns.why: hiding them defeats the trust model
colored cells alone are invisible to screen readers
linear compresses sub-2x gaps when a 80x outlier is present

preserves.behavior: BenchmarkIndex list view remains available via a toggle for mobile users
Compare page contract - selection emits URLs the Compare page already understands
Existing /results/:benchmark/ route - do not change URL pattern, only the rendered content
Existing manifest.json consumers - this TODO adds a new loader, does not remove the existing one

verifications.expected: imported and rendered as default view

verifications.description: Color function is pure and exported for testing

work_units.notes:
The current Compare.tsx calls find() to get the first QueryTiming
row for each query (Compare.tsx:107, :350). This returns the
cold-cache outlier when multiple measurement iterations exist (e.g.,
[16, 11, 11, 11] → 16ms displayed).

Fix: read `display_timings` (list[QueryDisplayTiming]) from the
detail JSON instead of scanning the raw `queries` array. The
`display_ms` value per query_id is the median of successful runs,
computed by the pipeline (see explorer-fix-read-model-contract).

Add a helper in src/lib/queryReduction.ts:
  `getDisplayMs(detail: DetailResult, queryId: string): number | null`
It reads `detail.display_timings.find(t => t.query_id === queryId)?.display_ms ?? null`.
Replace both find() call-sites in Compare.tsx with this helper.

This makes the matrix and the Compare page agree on what a query's
performance is - they will now both use the same canonical reduced
value from the pipeline.
work_units.summary: Fix Compare.tsx to use display_ms from DetailResult instead of first-row raw duration_ms
